- D5's claim about `~/.zshrc` sourcing `~/.zsh.d/*.zsh` before the non-interactive early-return guard, and `aliases.zsh` being a symlink to `~/.aliases`, both checked out exactly as stated against the real file.

# LENS A - the turned cube

## The seat

**The professional most affected: the solo operator whose interactive shell and `$HOME` *are* the production system.** Jeremy at a prompt on Tuesday, three weeks after this ships, in the middle of a different project, with no memory of this plan.

That seat is chosen because every artifact here lands in his live daily-use HOME (`~/.config/just/`, `~/.config/jjr/prompts/`, `~/.zsh.d/`), and one of them rebinds a command he already has installed at `/usr/local/bin/jq`. The blast radius is not a service or a repo, it is his shell, in every future session, on every project.

Runners-up considered and passed on:

- **The executing agent** (human or LLM running the plan). Affected, but only for one session. The plan is written well *for* this reader - waves, interfaces, executed checks. Its problems are not this reader's problems.
- **A teammate or the WSL box.** His team is non-technical and never touches this; WSL is a second install, not a downstream consumer. Real but thin.
- **A future maintainer folding this into a dotfiles repo.** Genuinely affected (see finding 4), but that is Jeremy in six months, which is the same seat with a longer time horizon. Folded in.

Environment claims below were checked against disk on this machine today, not recalled.

---

## Findings

### 1. Every launcher is a permanent, from-anywhere permission bypass, with no un-bypassed variant

- **finding:** All 15 public recipes bake in `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (claude) or `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (codex), and `just -g` makes them reachable from any cwd. There is no `cc-safe`, no opt-in, no way to launch these agents through this launcher *with* guardrails. The codex flag is the stronger of the two: it disables the sandbox, not just the approval prompts. The existing per-repo justfiles the plan copies this pattern from live in one known project directory; globalizing the recipes silently globalizes the flag to `~`, `/`, `~/Downloads`, and any repo he just cloned.
- **severity:** critical
- **rationale:** From my seat the whole point of the alias is that it becomes muscle memory. In three weeks I will type `jq cdx` in whatever directory I happen to be in without reading a recipe. If that directory is `$HOME`, I have handed an unsandboxed agent `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config`, and `~/.claude`. Today's per-repo justfiles at least made me `cd` somewhere deliberate first; that friction was doing safety work nobody noticed, and this plan removes it. The plan's Global constraints section lists path hygiene and model pinning but never once names this as a risk, and no human checkpoint covers it - Checkpoints A and C gate *spend*, not blast radius.
- **concrete suggested change:** Invert the default. Make the plain names (`cc`, `cdx`, `cc-content`, ...) carry no bypass flag, and add explicitly-named bypass variants (`cc-yolo`, `cdx-yolo`, or a `YOLO=1 jq cc` env gate) for the cases that need it. If keeping the bypass as default is a deliberate standing decision, then it belongs in the Settled decisions table as its own row with the blast radius written out, plus a `# WARNING:` comment line above each core recipe naming what the flag disables - not left as an unremarked implementation detail inside a one-line recipe body.

### 2. The `jq` collision is worse than "shadows the JSON tool", and the plan's containment rationale is factually wrong

- **finding:** Task 4 Step 4 records the collision as a report line only, and justifies containment with "zsh aliases do not expand in non-interactive scripts." That is false. Verified on this machine: a `zsh` script containing `alias jq="echo ALIAS-EXPANDED"` followed by `jq foo` prints `ALIAS-EXPANDED foo`. zsh expands aliases in scripts. What actually contains the blast is that non-interactive zsh does not source `~/.zshrc`, so the alias is never defined there - a different, more fragile property that the plan does not identify and therefore cannot protect. Separately, the interactive damage is not limited to "an error message": `just`'s short flags overlap jq's most common ones. From `just --help` on this machine, `-c` takes a command and **runs it**, `-e` opens the justfile in `$EDITOR`, `-f` reinterprets the next argument as a justfile, `-s`, `-n`, `-q` all exist. So `jq -c '.x' data.json` and `jq -e '.x' data.json` do something other than fail cleanly.
- **severity:** high
- **rationale:** I have jq installed at `/usr/local/bin/jq` and this ecosystem leans on it hard - `scripts/tracker.sh`, `skills/loop-setup/setup.sh`, and the `compare` / `pi-compare` recipes the plan itself cites all pipe through it. Those are safe because they are bash shebang recipes. What is not safe is me, at an interactive prompt, doing the single most ordinary thing in the world: `curl ... | jq -r '.x'`. Months from now I will get a `just` error about a recipe named `.x` and have zero recollection that I did this to myself, because the only place the decision is written down is a report I read once. The wrong stated rationale also means that if `~/.zshrc` ever gets sourced from a non-interactive context - or I add a `zsh -i -c` wrapper somewhere - the plan gives me no way to see the trap coming, since it thinks aliases are the safety mechanism when the sourcing rule is.
- **concrete suggested change:** Three things. (a) Correct the rationale in the plan to the real one: `~/.zshrc` is not sourced by non-interactive zsh, so the alias is undefined in scripts; drop the false claim about alias expansion. (b) Put the warning where I will actually find it - as a comment block in `~/.zsh.d/just.zsh` itself, naming the shadowed binary, its full path `/usr/local/bin/jq`, and the escape hatches (`\jq`, `command jq`, `/usr/local/bin/jq`) - so `type jq` plus one `cat` explains everything. (c) Reconsider the name. `j` is unused and free of this entire class of problem; if `jq` is kept for muscle memory, that is a decision that deserves its own Settled-decisions row acknowledging the `-c`/`-e`/`-f` flag overlap, not just the name overlap.

### 3. Multi-token pass-through is silently collapsed into one argument, which breaks exactly the flags I need most

- **finding:** `quote(args)` wraps the entire variadic string as a single shell word. Verified by running the plan's own recipe body against just 1.58.0: `just -n cc-content foo bar` renders `... 'foo bar'` - one argument, not two. A single-token flag survives (`just -n cc --resume` renders `'--resume'`), but any flag with a value does not. `jq cc --resume <session-id>` reaches claude as one positional string `--resume <session-id>`, and `jq cc-code --model opus` reaches it as `--model opus`. Neither errors loudly; claude treats it as an initial prompt. The plan's Task 3 acceptance check tests exactly one case - a single quoted prose prompt - and the "Why the recipe bodies look the way they do" section reasons only about prose prompts, never about flags.
- **severity:** high
- **rationale:** I lose sessions to quota limits constantly, so `claude --resume <id>` and `claude -c` are the two commands I reach for more than any other. This launcher is meant to become my default way in, and it quietly cannot do the thing I need most - and fails by *silently sending my session id to the model as a prompt* rather than by erroring. That is the worst failure shape: it looks like it worked. D4 in Settled decisions frames the choice as "bare `{{args}}` word-splits a quoted prompt", which is true, but the fix chosen trades one silent breakage for another and the plan never names the second one.
- **concrete suggested change:** Do not quote the variadic as one word. Use a bash-shebang core for all three programs (the shape already written as the option-(c) `_codex` body) with `exec claude ... "$@"` so real argv is preserved, or accept the split and document that a multi-word prose prompt must be passed as `jq cc-content "$(cat)"` or similar. Either way, add two cases to the Task 3 acceptance check: `just -g -n cc --resume abc123` must render `--resume` and `abc123` as separate tokens, and a two-word prose prompt must survive. Right now the check is a happy-path demo.

### 4. Nothing tells me how to undo this, and nothing in the artifacts points back at the plan

- **finding:** The plan writes to three separate locations under `$HOME` across three tasks in three waves, and contains no uninstall step, no manifest, and no recovery instructions for a half-applied state. If the session dies between Task 3 and Task 4 I have an orphan justfile and no alias. If it dies after Task 4 with a justfile that fails to parse, `jq` is broken in every new interactive shell I open and the recovery (`rm ~/.zsh.d/just.zsh`, or `unalias jq` in the current shell) is written down nowhere. The artifacts themselves carry no backreference: `~/.config/just/justfile` never names the plan or brief that produced it, so opening it in six months gives me recipe bodies with no provenance.
- **severity:** high
- **rationale:** Self-admitted novice-to-intermediate on shell, juggling many projects, routinely losing sessions to quota. This is precisely the profile that gets stranded by a half-applied HOME mutation, and the failure surfaces in the one place I cannot escape - a shell that starts wrong. The plan's Deferred section asserts "both artifacts are movable as whole units," which is a portability claim, not a rollback claim; there is no `rm` line anywhere in this document.
- **concrete suggested change:** Add an explicit uninstall block to the plan - the exact three-line `rm` sequence plus `unalias jq` for the already-open shell - and make it the first thing under "How to run", not an appendix. Add a header comment to `~/.config/just/justfile` and to `~/.zsh.d/just.zsh` giving the source plan path and date. Consider making Task 4 (the alias) the *last* thing installed and reversible in one command, which it nearly is already, and say so.

### 5. Task 3 deletes the codex verdict before Task 5 needs it, and the choice is never recorded anywhere durable

- **finding:** Task 1 produces `/tmp/codex-role-verdict.txt` and Task 3 Step 6 deletes it, stating "nothing else reads" it. Task 5 Step 4 then says "run the codex smoke matching the option Task 1 selected" and branches on option (a) versus option (c) - it needs that verdict, which is gone. Worse, the verdict lived only in `/tmp` and the resulting recipe body carries no comment saying which option was chosen or why, so the single paid probe in this entire plan produces no durable artifact.
- **severity:** medium
- **rationale:** Two costs from my seat. Immediately, an executor reaching Task 5 has to reverse-engineer the choice from the justfile body. More importantly for me: if the session dies between Task 3 and Task 5 - which is the normal case, not the edge case - the verdict is unrecoverable and the paid `codex exec` probe has to be re-run to resume. That is the exact resume failure I keep hitting, caused here by a cleanup step that runs one task too early. And six months out, when codex changes behavior, the justfile gives me no way to know whether `model_instructions_file` was chosen because it appends or accepted despite replacing.
- **concrete suggested change:** Move the verdict-file deletion from Task 3 Step 6 to Task 5 Step 6, alongside the other terminal cleanup. Independently, write the verdict into the justfile as a comment above `_codex` - one line, e.g. the verdict word, the date, and one clause of rationale - so the probe's result survives the loss of `/tmp` and of this plan document.

### 6. The role stubs are no-ops, so the brief's "immediately usable" outcome does not ship

- **finding:** Task 2 writes four files whose entire content is a marker token plus the line "Role: content. Stub only. Real role instructions are deferred." Real prompt content is explicitly deferred. So on day one, `jq cc-content` appends a system prompt that tells the model the role is a stub and gives it a test marker - functionally identical to `jq cc`, except with noise injected. The brief's End artifact section claims the result is "immediately usable for real content, design, and writing sessions"; the plan does not deliver that and does not flag the gap.
- **severity:** medium
- **rationale:** I will finish this build, see 15 green recipes and three passing smoke tests, and reasonably conclude the thing works. Then I will use `jq cc-content` for actual content work and get nothing - or slightly worse than nothing, since the appended text tells the model to disregard itself. The verification here proves the plumbing carries a file to the model, which is genuine and worth having, but the plan's success signal does not distinguish "plumbing works" from "launcher is useful", and I am the one who will conflate them.
- **concrete suggested change:** Either pull one real role prompt into scope so at least one combo is genuinely usable at ship time, or state plainly in the plan header and in the final report that all four roles are inert until the deferred prompt-authoring work lands, and drop the brief's "immediately usable" claim. Also reword the stub body so it does not read as an instruction to the model - a comment-style line, or marker-only, avoids priming a real session with self-negating text.

---

**One factual correction, offered as a note rather than a finding:** Task 2 Step 1 states `~/.config/jjr/` "already exists and holds `VOICE.md`, `OPINIONS.md`, `LEADERSHIP.md`, and `notebooklm.md`". `OPINIONS.md` is not there - the directory contains only `VOICE.md`, `LEADERSHIP.md`, and `notebooklm.md`. This does not affect the plan (Step 1 is a `mkdir -p`), but `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` `@`-references `~/.config/jjr/OPINIONS.md`, which means that reference is currently dangling. Separate problem, worth knowing.

The plan's Deferred section asserts "both artifacts are movable as whole units," which is a portability claim, not a rollback claim; there is no `rm` line anywhere in this document.

Add a header comment to `~/.config/just/justfile` and to `~/.zsh.d/just.zsh` giving the source plan path and date. Consider making Task 4 (the alias) the *last* thing installed and reversible in one command, which it nearly is already, and say so.

findings.title: The role stubs are no-ops, so the brief's "immediately usable" outcome does not ship
findings.rationale: I will finish this build, see 15 green recipes and three passing smoke tests, and reasonably conclude the thing works. Then I will use `jq cc-content` for actual content work and get nothing - or slightly worse than nothing, since the appended text tells the model to disregard itself. The verification here proves the plumbing carries a file to the model, which is genuine and worth having, but the plan's success signal does not distinguish "plumbing works" from "launcher is useful", and I am the one who will conflate them.
findings.suggested_change: Either pull one real role prompt into scope so at least one combo is genuinely usable at ship time, or state plainly in the plan header and in the final report that all four roles are inert until the deferred prompt-authoring work lands, and drop the brief's "immediately usable" claim. Also reword the stub body so it does not read as an instruction to the model - a comment-style line, or marker-only, avoids priming a real session with self-negating text.
findings.raw_block:
### 6. The role stubs are no-ops, so the brief's "immediately usable" outcome does not ship

- **finding:** Task 2 writes four files whose entire content is a marker token plus the line "Role: content. Stub only. Real role instructions are deferred." Real prompt content is explicitly deferred. So on day one, `jq cc-content` appends a system prompt that tells the model the role is a stub and gives it a test marker - functionally identical to `jq cc`, except with noise injected. The brief's End artifact section claims the result is "immediately usable for real content, design, and writing sessions"; the plan does not deliver that and does not flag the gap.
- **severity:** medium
- **rationale:** I will finish this build, see 15 green recipes and three passing smoke tests, and reasonably conclude the thing works. Then I will use `jq cc-content` for actual content work and get nothing - or slightly worse than nothing, since the appended text tells the model to disregard itself. The verification here proves the plumbing carries a file to the model, which is genuine and worth having, but the plan's success signal does not distinguish "plumbing works" from "launcher is useful", and I am the one who will conflate them.
- **concrete suggested change:** Either pull one real role prompt into scope so at least one combo is genuinely usable at ship time, or state plainly in the plan header and in the final report that all four roles are inert until the deferred prompt-authoring work lands, and drop the brief's "immediately usable" claim. Also reword the stub body so it does not read as an instruction to the model - a comment-style line, or marker-only, avoids priming a real session with self-negating text.

lenses.raw_text:
Both documents read in full, plus the eleven repo files the plan anchors to, and I re-derived the environment claims against disk.

---

## Findings

### 1. Task 8's stated premise is false against disk, and it breaks brief criterion 4

- **Severity:** critical
- **Rationale:** Task 8's behavior note says "None of the three carries a `## Next actions` section, so they are archived with a bulk transition line, exactly as Task 6 does." All three do carry one. Verified: `2026-08-22-wayfinder-sp-charting.md`, `2026-08-24-upgrade-path-orientation.md`, and `2026-08-30-pass1-firing.md` each have a heading and enumerated actions, but as `## Next actions, in recommended order` with `1. `/`2. ` numbered items, not `## Next actions` with `- ` items. So the premise is wrong twice over: the section exists, and it is in a shape the plan's parser (`the lines beginning "- " inside the ## Next actions section`) reads as zero actions. Following Task 8 as written would stamp a hand-written `action 0` line onto handoffs that have five real enumerable actions, and the criterion-4 acceptance check ("the older one is consumed and archived") cannot be met, because `handoff-log.sh state` on those files will not return `consumed`. This is also the only real-world sample of the section the plan's format was designed against, and the plan never looked at it.
- **Suggested change:** Re-derive Task 8 from the actual file contents before writing the plan's behavior notes, and decide explicitly whether `handoff-log.sh` matches the heading by prefix or exactly, and whether it enumerates `- ` only or `- ` plus `<n>. `. If the answer is that the existing corpus is unreadable, say so and route those three through the same bulk `action 0` path as Task 6 with the mismatch disclosed, rather than asserting the section is absent.

### 2. Derived state has a vacuous-truth hole: a section with zero parsed actions derives `consumed-unarchived`

- **Severity:** high
- **Rationale:** The state rules are "`live` when any action in `## Next actions` has no disposition line **or the section is absent**", otherwise `consumed`/`consumed-unarchived`. The plan covers "section absent" but not "section present, zero actions parsed". With zero actions, "every action has a disposition" is vacuously true, so the file derives `consumed-unarchived` and lint class h fires with exit 1. Every real handoff I looked at hits this case the moment the heading matches loosely: sys-prompts-cc's three (`## Next actions, in recommended order` with numbered items), and this repo's varied headings (`## Exact next actions`, `## Next`, `## Exact next commands`). Nothing in the plan or in the Task 2 test exercises the empty-enumeration case.
- **Suggested change:** Add "a section that parses to zero actions derives `live`" to the derived-state definition in Global constraints, and add an assertion for it to the Task 2 test fixture, because that is the shape the existing corpus actually has and a false class-h finding blocks the done-gate.

### 3. Task 2's verbatim test asserts a repo-relative archive announcement from an absolute input path

- **Severity:** high
- **Rationale:** The test passes `$h="$tmp/docs/handoffs/2026-09-10.I52.example-handoff.md"` (absolute, `$tmp` from `mktemp -d`) and then asserts `grep -q 'moved docs/handoffs/2026-09-10.I52.example-handoff.md to docs/archive/'`. The Interfaces section defines the output as `moved <src> to <dest>` and says nothing about relativizing, and nothing anywhere in the plan tells `handoff-log.sh` how to derive a repo root from a handoff path. A straightforward implementation that echoes the paths it was given prints the absolute form and fails this assertion. The executor's likely repair is an unstated prefix-strip hack invented at Step 3.
- **Suggested change:** Pin the announcement's path convention in the Interfaces contract (either "paths are printed exactly as given" and fix the test's grep, or "paths are printed relative to the git toplevel of the handoff" and say how that is resolved). Do not leave a verbatim test asserting a behavior the contract does not name.

### 4. Task 1's verbatim test relies on an unspecified tie-break among same-second open cards

- **Severity:** high
- **Rationale:** `log` and `close` target "the newest card whose `status:` is `open`, resolved by the `session:` timestamp", and `session:` is ISO-8601 to one-second granularity. The test's five `open` calls all complete inside the same second on any normal machine, and critically `card2` is opened and left open before the status-vocabulary loop runs, so during each loop iteration two cards are `open` with identical `session:` values. Whether `close "$s"` hits the probe card or `card2` is then decided by an unwritten tie-break, and the following `grep -qE "^status: $s\$" "$c"` fails if it guesses wrong. The test may pass today by accident of filename ordering (`.I52.seam-1-...` sorts before `.status-probe-...`), which is exactly the kind of green that rots.
- **Suggested change:** Specify the tie-break in the Global-constraints card-format block (for example, newest `session:` then newest filename, or reject when more than one card is open), and either close `card2` before the vocabulary loop or give each probe a distinct title, so the test discriminates the intended behavior rather than an accident.

### 5. The `done` lane and `docs/sessions/` are unbounded; the plan bounds only the tracker half

- **Severity:** high
- **Rationale:** `take-stock.sh --cards` emits "one `session` row per file in `docs/sessions/`" with no window, `board-cards.sh` turns each into a card, and `done`/`aborted` cards land in the `done` lane permanently. The closed-issue half of the same lane gets `DONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS=60`, which shows the plan understood the problem for issues and did not carry it across. Task 9 also adds a Sessions row to the Lanes table but adds nothing to `## Archive and graduation rules` (currently 1 to 6; the plan adds only rule 7 for handoffs), so `docs/sessions/` has no graduation path and lint class f is explicitly exempted from it. At one card per session across eight repos the `done` lane and the render loop grow without limit, and the board that seam 1 exists to fill becomes unreadable within weeks.
- **Suggested change:** Give session cards the same bounded lookback as closed issues (reuse `DONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` in `take-stock.sh` or in the `done` arm of `board-cards.sh`), and add an archive/graduation rule for `docs/sessions/` in Task 9 so the lane has a defined end state rather than only a defined start.

### 6. Task 10 propagates into seven repos with no clean-tree precondition and no rollback point

- **Severity:** high
- **Rationale:** `reconcile_config` replaces both `config/repo-state.md` and `config/conventions.md` with the render (setup.sh's own words: "accepting REPLACES both files with the renders above; any hand edits not shown as kept are lost"), and the carry-forward loop preserves only four keys. Task 10 Step 7 loops over seven repos with no `git status` check first, so any uncommitted config edit in a target repo is destroyed with no git recovery. This is sharpest for sys-prompts-cc, which Task 8 Step 7 deliberately leaves dirty and uncommitted ("Leave sys-prompts-cc's own commit to Jeremy"): Task 10 then writes into that same working tree, so the Task 8 archive moves and session card have no commit standing behind them when the re-render lands. I also confirmed this repo's own `config/repo-state.md` has drifted from a v6 render (key order differs and the `rubix-autorun values:` legend line is missing), so Step 6's re-render is a larger diff than the plan implies and its three `grep` checks would not catch a dropped line.
- **Suggested change:** Make a clean or committed working tree a stated precondition of each repo's roll, printed in the Step 5 checkpoint table alongside the template-version, and add "Jeremy has committed sys-prompts-cc" as an explicit dependency of Task 10 rather than an open loop from Task 8.

### 7. The per-action disposition machinery is never exercised on a real handoff in this run

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** I verified all 20 handoffs here have no `## Next actions` section. Task 6, Task 8, and Task 10 Step 10 therefore all hand-write `action 0` transition lines and hand-run `git mv`, bypassing `handoff-log.sh` entirely. `handoff-log.sh consume` is called by nothing in the plan except its own test, and the auto-archive-on-last-disposition path likewise only ever runs against a synthetic fixture. Brief criterion 1 is satisfied by a unit test and by nothing else. Compounding it, `action 0` is outside the 1..N range the script itself rejects, so the records the backfill writes are in a shape `handoff-log.sh actions` cannot read and `state` will report `live` for forever, including for files already in `docs/archive/`.
- **Suggested change:** Either give the backfill records a shape the tool can read back (and state what `state` returns for a bulk-backfilled archived file), or drop `consume` as a verb since `disposition` already covers the only success path and the refusal is a two-line guard. Then add one real end-to-end disposition to the run, most naturally the Task 7 handoff, so criterion 1 has a live proof and not only a fixture.

### 8. The all-suites-green gate inside each task breaks the parallel waves

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** The file-ownership sets in Wave 1 (Tasks 1, 2, 4) and Wave 4 (Tasks 7, 9) genuinely are disjoint, but every task ends with "run `tests/run.sh` and confirm no previously passing suite regressed" (Task 2 Step 6, Task 4 Step 5, Task 7 Step 6, Task 9 Step 7). `tests/run.sh` globs `tests/*/*.sh` over the whole worktree. Task 2's full-suite gate fires while Task 4 has `board-cards.sh` at 13 fields and `board-render-obsidian.sh` still at 12, so `tests/board/render.sh` fails and Task 2 blocks on damage it did not cause and cannot fix. The plan asserts parallelism on file ownership and never checks that the acceptance gates are also disjoint.
- **Suggested change:** Scope each in-wave regression gate to the suites the task can affect and move the single `tests/run.sh` all-green check to the wave boundary, or state that the waves are advisory and the tasks run serially.

### 9. Two of Task 5's marker assertions are vacuous, and the D9 suppression exception has no test

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** `[ "$(mark 'create/repoB#git')" = "" ]` passes against nothing: repoB's discovery row is `disc "$tmp/repoB" "create/repoB" 0 0`, so it is clean and conforming with one tracker card, and line 131's suppression drops its git card entirely. `mark` on a card_id that was never emitted prints the empty string. Separately, the plan's headline D9 design call is "a went-stale repo always gets its git card, so the existing clean-conforming suppression rule gains one exception", but repoA carries 2 uncommitted files, so it is never clean and the bypass branch is never taken by the test. The single novel piece of behavior D9 introduces ships untested.
- **Suggested change:** Add a fourth fixture repo that is clean, conforming, has a tracker card, and is `went-stale` per the take-stock stub, and assert its git card is emitted with `marker=went-stale`. Change the repoB assertion to something that discriminates, or delete it.

### 10. "Newest live handoff" has no tie-break, and Task 7 manufactures a same-day tie

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** The authoritative handoff is "the newest live one", resolved from filename dates at day granularity. Task 7 Step 3 writes `docs/handoffs/<today>.I52.seam1-next-thread.md` while `docs/handoffs/2026-09-07.I52.board-mvp-to-seam1-handoff.md` is still live (Task 6's table says "keep live", Task 10 Step 10 archives it). Today is 2026-09-07, so both share a date and the winner is undefined. Task 7 Step 4 asserts the report names the new one, and Task 7's acceptance check is brief criterion 2. This is the same missing tie-break as finding 4, at a different acceptance gate.
- **Suggested change:** Define the tie-break for equal-dated handoffs in the take-stock behavior notes (filename order or file mtime, stated), or have Task 7 archive the seam-1 handoff before writing the new one so no tie exists.

### 11. Task 10 Step 4 points at an updated `by-lane.base` that no task produces

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** Step 4 says "Copy the updated `assets/board/by-lane.base` into the live board home only if the marker property is wanted in the view ordering", but no task in the plan lists `assets/board/by-lane.base` under Files, and neither Task 4 nor Task 5 edits it. I read the shipped asset: all eight lane views already exist, and each view's `order` block lists `title, repo, staleness, health, last_work, position` with no `marker`. So the marker frontmatter key is written to every card note and surfaced nowhere in a view, and the only reason the plan gets away with it is the title-prefix workaround.
- **Suggested change:** Either give Task 4 explicit ownership of `assets/board/by-lane.base` and add `marker` to the view orders, or delete Step 4 and state plainly that the title prefix is the only surface, so the executor is not sent looking for an artifact that does not exist.

### 12. `went-stale` compares three different clock conventions at calendar-day granularity

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** Recorded-state timestamps are pinned UTC (`ISO-8601 UTC` everywhere in the card format), live-handoff contributions come from filename dates that were written in the author's local date, and "the newest commit's `YYYY-MM-DD`" is never pinned to a timezone at all, so it defaults to the committer's local zone in git. The went-stale verdict is a strict day comparison across those three. I confirmed the skew is live on this host right now: `date -u` reads 2026-09-08 while local time is 2026-09-07 evening. On US Eastern the error direction happens to be safe, but the plan does not know that and does not say so, and this comparison is the mechanism behind brief criterion 3.
- **Suggested change:** Pin the commit-date read to UTC explicitly in the take-stock behavior notes (`git log -1 --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%d` with `TZ=UTC`, or `--date=iso-strict` normalized), and say in one line which clock the handoff filename date is assumed to be in.

### 13. `list-closed` card rules are underspecified for the two label rules the open path applies

- **Severity:** moderate
- **Rationale:** Task 5 says closed-issue cards use "the same `card_id` and token rules as open tracker cards", but the open path at `board-cards.sh:103` also skips `wayfinder:*` outright, and line 115 rewrites the token to `B<n>` for `idea`. Neither is mentioned for the closed path. As written, a closed wayfinder map gets a `done` card, contradicting the `_health.md` line the plan leaves standing ("wayfinder:* issues get no card"), and a closed idea gets card_id `key#B<n>` in the `done` lane with no rule saying whether that is wanted.
- **Suggested change:** State the two label rules for closed issues in Task 5's Interfaces, and add one assertion for whichever behavior is chosen to the Task 5 test block, since the `_health.md` prose the same task rewrites makes a claim about wayfinder that the code would then contradict.

### 14. `docs/sessions/` is a new committed lane and is missing from the hardcodes sweep allowlist

- **Severity:** low
- **Rationale:** `tests/hardcodes/sweep.sh` fails any tracked file outside its explicit `ALLOW` list that contains `/Users/jjrdar`. `docs/reviews/` and `docs/handoffs/` are allowlisted; `docs/sessions/` is not, and the plan never adds it. Task 7 Step 2 tells the executor to log "one line per completed task so far", and this plan's own tasks are full of absolute paths (Task 8 Step 2 is a literal `/Users/jjrdar/...` invocation). One such log line committed into a session card turns `tests/hardcodes/sweep.sh` red, which every subsequent task's `tests/run.sh` gate then trips over.
- **Suggested change:** Add `docs/sessions/` to the sweep's `ALLOW` list as part of Task 1 or Task 9, and note it in the Global constraints beside the existing house-style rules, since a new committed lane is exactly the kind of addition that allowlist is designed to be updated for.

### 15. `take-stock.sh` is invoked inside `board-cards.sh`'s stdin-driven read loop without `</dev/null`

- **Severity:** low
- **Rationale:** `board-cards.sh` consumes the Discovery TSV via `while IFS= read -r line` on stdin, and Task 5 adds `( cd "$path" && "$TAKE_STOCK_CMD" . --cards )` inside that loop. Unlike the existing `"$TRACKER_CMD" list` call, take-stock shells out to `git log`, `date`, and one `handoff-log.sh state` per handoff on every iteration. Any one of those inheriting and reading stdin silently eats discovery rows, and the failure mode is missing repos rather than an error. The Task 5 test cannot catch it because its stub is a two-line `case` that reads nothing.
- **Suggested change:** Redirect the take-stock subshell's stdin from `/dev/null` and say so in the behavior note, for the same reason the existing code resolves `TRACKER_CMD` before the per-repo `cd`: the loop's invariants are not obvious from the call site.

### 16. The `rubix-autorun` carry-forward interpolates an unvalidated config value into a `sed` replacement

- **Severity:** low
- **Rationale:** The fix in Task 9 is `sed -E "s|^rubix-autorun:.*|rubix-autorun: $ra|"` where `$ra` is whatever follows the key in the target repo's config. A `|`, `&`, or backslash in that value corrupts the replacement or the whole expression, and this runs during Task 10's write into eight repos, which is the least recoverable moment in the plan. The valid vocabulary is exactly three words and is already documented in the template's legend line, so validating is a three-arm `case`.
- **Suggested change:** Validate `$ra` against `ask|off|on` before substituting and fall back to leaving the rendered default in place otherwise, and state where in `reconcile_config` the substitution is inserted, because it must run before the `diff -u` the human reviews or the approved diff is not the file that gets written.

---

## Pressure points I checked that came back sound

The 13-field widening is fully coordinated: the only Card TSV consumers in the repo are `board-render-obsidian.sh` and the two board tests, and `board.sh` only pipes.
I confirmed the `IFS=$US read -r -a f` unpacking yields `f[12]` correctly for both an empty and a populated 13th field on the stock `/bin/bash` 3.2 here, and that awk counts a trailing-tab row as `NF=13`.
Every line-number anchor in the plan matches the current files, including the four in `tracker.sh` and the exact 318-321 carry-forward range in `setup.sh`.
The BSD date forms used in the tests (`-v-30H`, `-v+1d`, `-j -f`) all work here, and `date -d` correctly does not, so the BSD-first ordering is right.
The plan's environment claims are accurate: the four-finding lint baseline reproduces exactly, the 20 handoff filenames match the Task 6 table one for one, and the eight-repo template-version table is correct including the `pokemine`-at-6 correction.
The `config/conventions.md` drift is exactly the five-line `rubix-autorun` block the plan says it is, so Task 9's warning about the bare `cp` is real and correctly handled.

findings.title: Task 1's verbatim test relies on an unspecified tie-break among same-second open cards
findings.rationale: `log` and `close` target "the newest card whose `status:` is `open`, resolved by the `session:` timestamp", and `session:` is ISO-8601 to one-second granularity. The test's five `open` calls all complete inside the same second on any normal machine, and critically `card2` is opened and left open before the status-vocabulary loop runs, so during each loop iteration two cards are `open` with identical `session:` values. Whether `close "$s"` hits the probe card or `card2` is then decided by an unwritten tie-break, and the following `grep -qE "^status: $s\$" "$c"` fails if it guesses wrong. The test may pass today by accident of filename ordering (`.I52.seam-1-...` sorts before `.status-probe-...`), which is exactly the kind of green that rots.
findings.suggested_change: Specify the tie-break in the Global-constraints card-format block (for example, newest `session:` then newest filename, or reject when more than one card is open), and either close `card2` before the vocabulary loop or give each probe a distinct title, so the test discriminates the intended behavior rather than an accident.

findings.title: The `done` lane and `docs/sessions/` are unbounded; the plan bounds only the tracker half
findings.rationale: `take-stock.sh --cards` emits "one `session` row per file in `docs/sessions/`" with no window, `board-cards.sh` turns each into a card, and `done`/`aborted` cards land in the `done` lane permanently. The closed-issue half of the same lane gets `DONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS=60`, which shows the plan understood the problem for issues and did not carry it across. Task 9 also adds a Sessions row to the Lanes table but adds nothing to `## Archive and graduation rules` (currently 1 to 6; the plan adds only rule 7 for handoffs), so `docs/sessions/` has no graduation path and lint class f is explicitly exempted from it. At one card per session across eight repos the `done` lane and the render loop grow without limit, and the board that seam 1 exists to fill becomes unreadable within weeks.
findings.suggested_change: Give session cards the same bounded lookback as closed issues (reuse `DONE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` in `take-stock.sh` or in the `done` arm of `board-cards.sh`), and add an archive/graduation rule for `docs/sessions/` in Task 9 so the lane has a defined end state rather than only a defined start.

findings.title: Task 10 propagates into seven repos with no clean-tree precondition and no rollback point
findings.rationale: `reconcile_config` replaces both `config/repo-state.md` and `config/conventions.md` with the render (setup.sh's own words: "accepting REPLACES both files with the renders above; any hand edits not shown as kept are lost"), and the carry-forward loop preserves only four keys. Task 10 Step 7 loops over seven repos with no `git status` check first, so any uncommitted config edit in a target repo is destroyed with no git recovery. This is sharpest for sys-prompts-cc, which Task 8 Step 7 deliberately leaves dirty and uncommitted ("Leave sys-prompts-cc's own commit to Jeremy"): Task 10 then writes into that same working tree, so the Task 8 archive moves and session card have no commit standing behind them when the re-render lands. findings.title: The per-action disposition machinery is never exercised on a real handoff in this run
findings.rationale: I verified all 20 handoffs here have no `## Next actions` section. Task 6, Task 8, and Task 10 Step 10 therefore all hand-write `action 0` transition lines and hand-run `git mv`, bypassing `handoff-log.sh` entirely. `handoff-log.sh consume` is called by nothing in the plan except its own test, and the auto-archive-on-last-disposition path likewise only ever runs against a synthetic fixture. Brief criterion 1 is satisfied by a unit test and by nothing else. Compounding it, `action 0` is outside the 1..N range the script itself rejects, so the records the backfill writes are in a shape `handoff-log.sh actions` cannot read and `state` will report `live` for forever, including for files already in `docs/archive/`.
findings.suggested_change: Either give the backfill records a shape the tool can read back (and state what `state` returns for a bulk-backfilled archived file), or drop `consume` as a verb since `disposition` already covers the only success path and the refusal is a two-line guard. Then add one real end-to-end disposition to the run, most naturally the Task 7 handoff, so criterion 1 has a live proof and not only a fixture.

findings.title: The all-suites-green gate inside each task breaks the parallel waves
findings.rationale: The file-ownership sets in Wave 1 (Tasks 1, 2, 4) and Wave 4 (Tasks 7, 9) genuinely are disjoint, but every task ends with "run `tests/run.sh` and confirm no previously passing suite regressed" (Task 2 Step 6, Task 4 Step 5, Task 7 Step 6, Task 9 Step 7). `tests/run.sh` globs `tests/*/*.sh` over the whole worktree. Task 2's full-suite gate fires while Task 4 has `board-cards.sh` at 13 fields and `board-render-obsidian.sh` still at 12, so `tests/board/render.sh` fails and Task 2 blocks on damage it did not cause and cannot fix. The plan asserts parallelism on file ownership and never checks that the acceptance gates are also disjoint.
findings.suggested_change: Scope each in-wave regression gate to the suites the task can affect and move the single `tests/run.sh` all-green check to the wave boundary, or state that the waves are advisory and the tasks run serially.

findings.title: `went-stale` compares three different clock conventions at calendar-day granularity
findings.rationale: Recorded-state timestamps are pinned UTC (`ISO-8601 UTC` everywhere in the card format), live-handoff contributions come from filename dates that were written in the author's local date, and "the newest commit's `YYYY-MM-DD`" is never pinned to a timezone at all, so it defaults to the committer's local zone in git. The went-stale verdict is a strict day comparison across those three. I confirmed the skew is live on this host right now: `date -u` reads 2026-09-08 while local time is 2026-09-07 evening. On US Eastern the error direction happens to be safe, but the plan does not know that and does not say so, and this comparison is the mechanism behind brief criterion 3.
findings.suggested_change: Pin the commit-date read to UTC explicitly in the take-stock behavior notes (`git log -1 --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%d` with `TZ=UTC`, or `--date=iso-strict` normalized), and say in one line which clock the handoff filename date is assumed to be in.

lenses.raw_text:
## Seat

I'm sitting as **Jeremy, the solo repo owner**, who lives with this convention across every future session in 8 repos and two hosts, absorbs the three human checkpoints, and inherits whatever this plan bakes into the fleet's schema. Runners-up I considered and set aside: the fresh AI agent session that actually executes the doctrine each time (it bears the mechanical tax directly, but has no standing to object - Jeremy does); and Jeremy's WSL-host self, who inherits a fleet-wide schema decision made without his 1,528-line uncommitted design in hand (folded into finding 5 below rather than given its own seat, since it's really Jeremy paying that cost on a delay).

## Findings

**1. The session-card doctrine is invisible to a fresh agent's actual read path.**
Severity: critical.
Rationale: I read `/Users/jjrdar/create/loops/loop-stack-session/CLAUDE.md` - it names only `config/repo-state.md` and `config/context-map.md` as what a fresh agent reads. I read `config/context-map.md` in full - it indexes `docs/git-guide.md` for "git conventions" but never points at `config/conventions.md` or anything session-related. Task 9 adds the "Session records" and "Handoff lifecycle" doctrine sections only to `config/conventions.template.md`, and never touches `CLAUDE.md` or `context-map.md`. I also confirmed the *existing* "done-gate" rule (rule 6 in `config/conventions.md`, "declaring a task... runs `scripts/lifecycle-lint.sh .` first") already suffers this same gap today - the plan doubles down on that blind spot rather than closing it. Since nothing enforces `session-card.sh open` as literally step one, and the whole feature's value proposition is "a quota-killed session still leaves one card," a session that never reads `conventions.md` leaves zero trace, silently defeating the point.
Concrete change: add one line to `CLAUDE.md` (or `context-map.md`) in Task 9 - "every session opens a session card first; see conventions.md Session records" - so the convention sits on the two files a fresh agent is told to read, not on a third file nothing points to.

**2. No lint class validates session cards; only handoffs get enforcement.**
Severity: high.
Rationale: I grepped `scripts/lifecycle-lint.sh` for its class list (a through g) - none touches `docs/sessions/`, and `docs/sessions/` is explicitly exempted from class f. Handoffs get class h (a done-gate-failing check for exactly this kind of drift); session cards get nothing. A card never opened, a hand-edited card with a typo'd status (`in-progress` instead of `open`), or a card left open past 24 hours all fail silently - no lint finding, no board marker in the never-opened case.
Concrete change: extend `take-stock.sh`'s report or add a lint class that flags a session with recent commits but zero session card, so non-compliance is visible somewhere instead of only manifesting as a missing card nobody asked about.

**3. Handoff consumption has no batch verb - the "recording tax" cap the brief promises doesn't cover it.**
Severity: high.
Rationale: the brief pins "the recording tax is capped at that one card [session card]; anything derivable comes from take-stock derivation." But Task 2's `handoff-log.sh disposition <handoff> <n> <disposition> [note]` is strictly per-action, and nothing in the plan defines a bulk verb. A handoff with 5 next-actions costs 5 manual invocations to archive. That tax is real, recurring on every future handoff in 8 repos, and explicitly uncapped by the brief's own language.
Concrete change: add a bulk verb (e.g. `handoff-log.sh disposition-all <handoff> <executed|superseded>`) so archiving a handoff isn't O(actions) manual calls.

**4. Task 6's human checkpoint bundles two independent decisions into one ask.**
Severity: high.
Rationale: verified in the plan text, Task 6 Step 3: after presenting the 20-row backfill disposition table for confirmation, it says "Ask one second question in the same breath" - whether to also archive two class-a-flagged plan files now or leave them live. A "confirmed" answer to the first risks being read as covering the second, and an edit to one row of the 20 could get conflated with the separate archive-timing call.
Concrete change: split into two sequential prompts/checkpoints so approving the backfill table can never be read as also deciding the unrelated archive-now-vs-later question.

**5. The WSL host's real design is bypassed by a "ships first, wins" rule rather than reconciled.**
Severity: moderate.
Rationale: the brief's own "Known vs guessed" section states the 5-status vocabulary and session-card key set are "guessed" from one-line summaries, and if the uncommitted 1,528-line WSL plan disagrees, "the vocabulary here wins because it ships first." This plan then propagates that schema into scripts, the Card TSV, and `board-cards.sh` across 8 repos before that plan is ever actually read. If it disagrees materially, reconciling means a second schema wave across the whole fleet plus retrofitting cards already written under the wrong shape - and it silently discards work Jeremy already did on the other host.
Concrete change: before Task 10's propagation, actually pull and diff the WSL plan's full text against D9/D13, or mark the fleet-wide roll as provisional until that reconciliation happens.

**6. DIED_MID_WORK_HOURS=24 will likely fire as noise given Jeremy's actual work rhythm.**
Severity: moderate.
Rationale: the plan hardcodes `DIED_MID_WORK_HOURS=24` (confirmed in Global constraints and Task 3). Combined with finding 1/2 (open/close discipline unenforced), a normal overnight-plus-a-day resume after a quota death - which is stated as his regular pattern, not an edge case - will surface as "died-mid-work" indistinguishably from a genuinely abandoned session. There's no cheap signal separating "will resume tomorrow" from "actually dead."
Concrete change: no code change is necessarily required, but this should be named as a decision point before propagation rather than discovered as board noise afterward.

**7. Handoff archive collisions have no automatic recovery; session cards do.**
Severity: moderate.
Rationale: Task 1 gives session cards an automatic `-2` suffix on filename collision. Task 2's `handoff-log.sh` archive path, on a destination collision, prints `<dest> already exists; left at <src>` and exits 6 with no retry or rename mechanism named anywhere in the plan - the file is stuck `consumed-unarchived` (a lint-failing state) until someone manually intervenes.
Concrete change: either auto-suffix the archive destination on collision (matching the session-card convention) or document the manual recovery command directly in the new conventions doctrine.

**8. "Log after each meaningful step" is undefined judgment with no floor.**
Severity: low-moderate.
Rationale: the only cadence guidance anywhere (Task 9's doctrine text) is "after each meaningful step" - no minimum, no lint check tying it back. Criterion 7 ("the card answers 'where did I leave off' without reconstruction") depends entirely on this undefined judgment being exercised consistently across every future session and every agent/model that runs one.
Concrete change: give the doctrine one concrete cadence rule (e.g., "log at minimum once per commit") so criterion 7 has a fair chance of passing on the first real session rather than depending on unwritten habit.

**9. Task 10's own propagation loop - the highest-risk task in the plan - has no incremental session-card logging, so a mid-loop death recreates the exact failure this feature exists to prevent.**
Severity: high.
Rationale: verified in Task 10 Steps 6-8: rolling `template-version` 7 into 7 external repos is a live, interactive, per-repo diff-review loop, explicitly told to run "one repo at a time rather than as an unattended loop." No step in that loop calls `scripts/session-card.sh log` per repo, and the propagation runbook (`docs/reviews/...propagation-runbook.md`) is only written at Step 8, after the entire loop completes. If the session executing this task dies after rolling, say, 4 of 7 repos (a live risk given quota limits and 7 rounds of interactive confirmation), neither the open session card nor a runbook records which repos are done - recovery requires manually re-checking `config/repo-state.md` in each of the 7 repos, i.e. exactly the reconstruction burden the whole feature is built to eliminate.
Concrete change: add `scripts/session-card.sh log "<repo> rolled to v7, lint <pass/fail>"` inside the per-repo loop in Task 10 Step 7, so a mid-propagation death leaves a card that names which repos are already done.

Nate's posts link ~147 Notion prompt-pack pages (142 `www.notion.so/product-templates/...`, 7 `product-templates.notion.site/...`).
Notion is a JS SPA, so the scraper's raw-HTTP `download_text` gets only the JS shell - a `rebuild` with the nate-notion config entries whitelisted would create ~149 junk notes.

name: mocked-exception-shapes-lie
description: "Test doubles must raise the REAL exception type - CalledProcessError hides stderr, RuntimeError mocks masked a live 429-detection gap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a6fd098f-6d47-4aaf-9dd6-5011bb6ee401
---

When a test fakes a subprocess failure, raise the exception the code path actually produces, not a convenient RuntimeError.
`subprocess.CalledProcessError.__str__` shows only "returned non-zero exit status N" - stderr is on `e.stderr`, invisible to `str(e)` matching.
The twitter-429 loop (2026-07-26) shipped green with a test faking `RuntimeError("HTTP 429")` for a thread failure; live HC1 showed the real `CalledProcessError` never exposed the 429, so `_is_rate_limited(str(e))` was blind (fixed in 701359d by raising stderr explicitly).

**Why:** mocked exception shapes are part of the contract under test; a wrong shape validates dead code paths.
**How to apply:** when a plan's test fakes a failure crossing a subprocess/API boundary, check what `str(e)` of the REAL exception carries; prefer making the production code normalize errors at the boundary (raise RuntimeError(stderr) at the call site) so tests and callers see one shape. Jeremy's E2E-repro rule ([[rubix-second-pass-value]] adjacent) is what catches these - keep HC live-repro gates even for fully-tested loops.

Also: batching both plans into 2 dispatches (one per lens) instead of 4 halved quota with no quality loss.

# Handoff: Rubix re-review of the GitLab plan - 23 findings, none applied yet

Date: 2026-08-09
Session: /loop-plan Rubix review (re-run) of `docs/plans/2026-08-09-gitlab-glab-support-plan.md`
State: findings recorded and verified; superseded 2026-08-09 (same day, later session) - all 23 findings were applied to the plan with findings 8 and 17 narrowed as recorded below, the prior handoff's blessing was corrected, and the brief's criteria 8-10 were restated; the plan's Review record carries the third entry

## Where things stand

The plan is unchanged on disk.
Two fresh-context lenses reviewed it, produced 25 raw findings, and those dedupe to 23.
I added 3 of my own and verified every load-bearing claim from both lenses against the repo before recording it here.
Nothing has been edited, so the next session can apply any subset without reconciling partial work.

| Artifact | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Plan under review | `docs/plans/2026-08-09-gitlab-glab-support-plan.md` (1,689 lines) |
| Source brief | `docs/briefs/2026-08-09-gitlab-glab-support-brief.md` |
| Prior handoff | `docs/handoffs/2026-08-09-gitlab-plan-ready.md` |
| This review | recorded here only; no plan revision, no commit |

This is the plan's **second** Rubix review.
The first ran before the bloat review cut the decision ledger, the `cksum` fingerprints, the version constants, and the setup-side migration offer.
That cut removed roughly 240 lines and changed Task 4's whole idempotence story, so re-reviewing the current text was worth doing rather than trusting the earlier round.
Both lenses were blind to this conversation and to the prior review record beyond what the plan itself states.

## How the review ran

Two read-only subagents, dispatched in parallel, each holding only the plan, the brief, and read access to the repo.

- **Lens A, the turned cube.** Told to enumerate the professionals downstream of the artifact, take the single most affected seat, and review what living with the plan would be like from it. It chose *the person re-running `loop-setup` in an already-settled repo he did not intend to change*, with runners-up being the teammate whose shared GitLab project receives the Task 7 smoke issues, and the agent running forge's vendored `gen-mirrors.sh` after a declined drift refresh.
- **Lens B, the scrambled start.** No seat and no sympathy: best practice for Bash CLI tooling, shell test harnesses, and idempotent setup scripts. Told to trace the plan's verbatim test scripts as code and to test the plan's on-disk claims rather than accept them.

Both ran on Opus.
Lens B would normally be a candidate for Fable given that this plan writes to a live shared corporate instance, but the global instructions bar Fable from ever being a worker, so Opus took both seats.

**Verification method.** I did not accept either lens on its word.
I re-derived the candidate count by extracting the shipped `is_excluded` and `is_candidate` predicates and running them over the real tree, confirmed the `find` empty-array behavior by running it, and read every cited line on disk.
Every claim recorded below survived that pass.
Where a lens was wrong, it is marked as part-declined with the reason.

## The blocking finding

With Task 4 ungating the import sweep, **every candidate the existing scan roots produce in this repo is a permanent design document.**

Re-derived rather than recalled:

```
current roots (docs .planning .ralph .scratch/*/issues) = 7 candidates
  docs/plans/2026-08-04-tracker-mode-plan.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-04-tracker-mode-plan_loop.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-07-loop-setup-reconcile-plan.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-08-audit-sweep-plan.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-08-audit-sweep-plan_loop.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-08-loop-improve-plan.md
  docs/plans/2026-08-09-gitlab-glab-support-plan.md    <- the plan itself
new root pass (Task 4)                                = 2 candidates
  PLAN.md
  fixing-agent-errors.md
TOTAL = 9
```

`is_excluded` at `skills/loop-setup/setup.sh:160` covers `docs/issues/*`, `docs/handoffs/*`, `docs/reviews/*`, `docs/briefs/*`, and `docs/archive/*`, and never `docs/plans/*`.
Task 4 then adds a `git mv` to `docs/archive/` behind the same confirmation as the import.
Under `LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1` that whole sequence is silent.

Two things make this worse than a nuisance.
`config/repo-state.md:64-65` makes plan archival a governed action with its own rules ("A brief archives when its plan archives; they travel together"), so the sweep would be reaching into a lane it does not own.
And `docs/briefs/*` is already excluded while `docs/plans/*` is not, which means the omission is an accident of when the sweep could not reach a github repo, not a decision.

**This was recorded and blessed in the prior handoff.**
Lines 41-42 of `docs/handoffs/2026-08-09-gitlab-plan-ready.md` state that ungating the sweep surfaces 9 candidates "including `PLAN.md` and this repo's own plan files" and call that "expected".
Two independent lenses, given no knowledge of that sentence, both flagged it as a defect.
That disagreement is the single most important thing in this document: the count was measured but never classified.

Two side effects of the same measurement.
The plan's pre-root-scan count of `6` at lines 49 and 1093 is wrong; the true figure is 7.
And Task 4's test fixture at plan line 974 uses `docs/some-plan.md` as a *wanted* candidate, which encodes the wrong intent into the suite that is supposed to gate the behavior.

## All 23 findings

Severity is the reviewing lens's, kept as given.
"Verdict" is mine.

| #  | Finding                                                                          | Lens | Sev  | Verdict               |
| -- | ---                                                                              | ---  | ---  | ---                   |
| 1  | `docs/plans/*` unexcluded; sweep offers and archives 7 live plan docs             | A+B  | crit | Revise                |
| 2  | Archive move has no repo-boundary and no destination-collision guard              | A+B  | high | Revise                |
| 3  | Root `find` pass collides with the empty-`roots` guard; degrades to full-tree scan | B    | high | Revise                |
| 4  | `LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE` gate is unexpressible as specified; `ask()` cannot signal it | B    | high | Revise                |
| 5  | `--dry-run-remote` loses its no-remote-calls guarantee                            | A+B  | high | Revise                |
| 8  | Mode-switch offer has no acknowledgment path; reverses a documented contract      | A    | high | Revise (narrowed)     |
| 14 | `backlog-group` check is exit-0 only; a too-wide group passes identically          | A    | high | Revise                |
| 15 | Declined `gen-mirrors.sh` drift refresh leaves forge disclosing GitHub falsely    | A    | high | Revise                |
| 6  | `{{BACKLOG_GROUP}}` renders a broken `glab` line into every github/local config    | B    | med  | Revise                |
| 7  | `render_github`'s hardcoded "(github or local)" sentence never widened             | B    | med  | Revise                |
| 9  | Sweep runs after the mirror render, so a run that files N issues leaves them stale | A    | med  | Revise                |
| 10 | "nothing to do" counter covers 2 of 4 offer sources                               | A    | med  | Revise                |
| 11 | Tasks 3/4/5 gate on one new suite each while all three edit `setup.sh`            | B    | med  | Revise                |
| 12 | `template-version: 2` stamped on a config that is not a v2 render                 | A+B  | med  | Revise                |
| 13 | Task 7 Step 4's fallback reopens a committed Task 1 and breaks its assertion      | B    | med  | Revise                |
| 16 | Step 7b cleanup rests on two never-verified `glab` commands                       | A    | med  | Revise                |
| 18 | Task 3 scenario B's title contradicts its own fixture                            | B    | med  | Revise (comment only) |
| 21 | A second github-only assertion is untouched by any task and ungrepped by any test | mine | med  | Revise                |
| 17 | New `is_excluded` names are called "root basenames" but match at any depth        | A+B  | low  | Revise (part-decline) |
| 19 | Task 5's "default is still github" assertion passes vacuously                     | B    | low  | Revise                |
| 20 | `SKILL.md:29` stale across Tasks 3-5 until Task 6 fixes it                        | B    | low  | Revise                |
| 22 | Task 6's line references for `config/repo-state.md` are off by one                | mine | low  | Revise                |
| 23 | Plan lines 49 and 1093 carry a stale candidate count of 6                        | mine | low  | Revise                |

## Specifics and rationale

### High severity

**1. `docs/plans/*` unexcluded.**
Covered in full above.
Suggested change: add `docs/plans/*` to the `is_excluded` prefix case in Task 4 step a, rename the test fixture off a plan filename, restate the steady-state count, and record that plan and brief archival stays owned by the Archive-and-graduation rules.

**2. The archive move has no guards.**
Task 4 step a (plan line 1113) specifies only `mkdir -p docs/archive`, then `git mv` when the file is tracked else `mv`.
There is no `-n`, no existence check, and no check that the candidate path is inside the repo.
`skills/loop-setup/setup.sh:33` accepts `--scan <dir>` with no in-tree requirement, and `tests/loop-setup/import.sh:68` already runs `setup.sh --scan "$EXTRA"` where `EXTRA="$(mktemp -d)"`, under `LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1`, with `$EXTRA/extra-plan.md` matching the `plan` keyword.
So the first run of the existing suite after Task 4 lands would `mv` a file out of an unrelated directory into the sandbox repo, and the suite would stay green because it never asserts that `$EXTRA/extra-plan.md` survives.
Separately, two candidates sharing a basename collapse onto one `docs/archive/<name>.md` and the first is destroyed with no message.
Suggested change: skip the move when the destination exists and say so, and skip the archive offer entirely for any candidate whose normalized path is absolute or starts with `../`.

**3. The root `find` pass collides with the empty-`roots` guard.**
`setup.sh:178` is `[ "${#roots[@]}" -gt 0 ] || return 0`, which exists because `find "${roots[@]}"` with an empty array is unsafe.
I confirmed the failure mode by running it: `bash -c 'set -uo pipefail; a=(); find "${a[@]}" -maxdepth 0'` prints `.`, so GNU find silently defaults to the entire tree.
Task 4 step a says only "merged with the existing recursive `find`" and never mentions the guard, so the obvious implementation of a repo with no `docs/` directory is a recursive scan of everything.
Note that `setup.sh:177` already uses the `${SCAN_ROOTS[@]+"${SCAN_ROOTS[@]}"}` idiom for exactly this hazard, which is the in-repo pattern to follow.
Suggested change: run the root pass unconditionally, keep the recursive pass behind the existing guard, and replace the function-level early return with an empty-candidate-list return.

**4. The `LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE` gate is unexpressible as specified.**
Plan lines 1101-1104 say the per-item confirmation "is not satisfied by `LOOP_ASSUME_YES` alone when `MODE` is `github` or `gitlab`" while "local mode and interactive per-item answers are unaffected".
`ask()` at `setup.sh:8-13` returns 0 for `LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1` and for an interactive `y` with no signal distinguishing them.
An implementer with zero context has two readings, and the wrong one (gate on `MODE` being remote) breaks the interactive path the plan promises to leave alone, including Task 7 Steps 2 and 3 in forge.
Task 4's test only exercises the non-interactive path, so the wrong reading passes.
Suggested change: state the condition literally, `[ "${LOOP_ASSUME_YES:-0}" = 1 ] && [ "${LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE:-0}" != 1 ]`.

**5. `--dry-run-remote` stops meaning what it says.**
`setup.sh:224-234` scopes the entire remote finalize on `DRY_REMOTE=1`, and `skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:50` documents the flag as skipping remote calls "instead of calling gh".
The new sweep gate keys on `MODE` and `LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE` with no `DRY_REMOTE` term, so `--dry-run-remote LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1 LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE=1` files real issues.
Existing dry-run tests do not set `LOOP_ASSUME_YES`, so nothing catches it and the next test author walks into it.
The plan's own review record cut a `DRY_REMOTE` interaction from the migration offer and never applied the same thought to the sweep.
Suggested change: add `[ "$DRY_REMOTE" -eq 0 ]` to the remote-creation condition, print the skip, and correct `SKILL.md:50` in Task 6.

**8. The mode-switch offer has no acknowledgment path.**
Plan line 883 makes a declined switch deliberately non-durable, justified at line 70 by "declines are the rare case once accepts self-archive".
That reasoning is sound for imports and false here: a declined mode switch has no archiving equivalent, so it is the one offer with unbounded repeat and no off switch.
It also reverses a shipped contract: `skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:16` says setup "skips the question entirely (idempotent, never re-asks)" and `:39` says "a declared mode is never re-asked", while `config/repo-state.md:58` actively tells users to choose local deliberately for branched work.
Task 3's own test asserts only the easy half, that an agreeing repo is never nagged (plan line 800).
See the narrowing note below for what I would and would not take here.

**14. The `backlog-group` check cannot fail informatively.**
Plan line 103 declined a reviewer's premise that a top-level group may be unusable on a university-wide instance, and adopted an exit-0 check instead.
The brief records at line 121 that the live group query returns `[]`.
An empty result set makes exit 0 pass identically for a correctly scoped group and for a university-wide one that will later pull other teams' `idea` issues into this repo's declared backlog view.
Plan lines 1592-1593 treat non-zero as the only failure signal, so the wrong-but-working case is unobservable, and the brief itself bins top-level grouping as **Guessed** at lines 143-145.
Suggested change: assert that every returned project path begins with `university-advancement/crm`, and name the fallback derivation as the action on any foreign project.

**15. A declined drift refresh leaves forge lying about its own provenance.**
The drift refresh is per file and declinable at `setup.sh:75-87`, and Task 7 Step 2 presents those refreshes as offers without marking any required.
Task 2's fix lives only in loop-stack's copy of `gen-mirrors.sh`; the vendored copy defaults `SRC_LABEL="GitHub issues"` for every non-local mode at `scripts/gen-mirrors.sh:84-87`.
So accepting the gitlab mode switch while declining the `gen-mirrors.sh` refresh produces mirrors that disclose GitHub as the source of truth on a GitLab repo, in a file whose entire purpose is disclosure, in the exact repo the plan ships to.
Suggested change: have the gitlab finalize fail with a named fix when the target repo's `gen-mirrors.sh` does not contain `GitLab issues`, and mark the `tracker.sh` and `gen-mirrors.sh` refreshes as required for gitlab mode in Task 7 Step 2.

### Medium severity

**6. `{{BACKLOG_GROUP}}` leaks into github and local configs.**
The "Backlog cross-repo view" lines sit at `config/repo-state.template.md:33`, well before `## Local tracker` at line 45, so they survive `render_github`'s heading strip at `setup.sh:96-102`.
Task 3 step e then has `render_local` substitute `n/a (local tracker)` and `render_github` substitute the derived group with "empty is acceptable", producing `glab issue list --group n/a (local tracker) --label idea` in every local config and `glab issue list --group  --label idea` plus a bare `backlog-group:` line in every github config.
`tests/loop-setup/reconcile.sh` diffs two identical renders, so nothing catches it.
Suggested change: have `render_github` and `render_local` drop the gitlab backlog-view lines and the `backlog-group:` line outright, using the same `index($0, ...)`/`next` mechanism already used for "Render it into".

**7. `render_github`'s hardcoded sentence is never widened.**
`setup.sh:99` emits the literal `The tracker backend (github or local) is declared in the \`tracker:\` key below.`
Task 3 step a widens template lines 5 and 23, and step e widens only `render_gitlab`'s replacement.
So every github-rendered config would say "(github or local)" while the template it came from says "(github, gitlab, or local)", in the same file Task 6 exists to de-github-ify, and no suite greps a rendered github config for that sentence.
Suggested change: add the one-line update to `setup.sh:99` in Task 3 step e.

**9. The sweep files issues after the mirrors are rendered.**
`setup.sh:235` and `:238` run `gen-mirrors.sh`, and `:240` runs `reconcile_import` afterwards.
In local mode the staleness at least announces itself, because `scripts/tracker.sh:73` emits "note: ISSUES.md/BACKLOG.md now stale" from `local_create`; the github and gitlab create paths emit nothing.
Task 4 makes the sweep backend-agnostic without moving or repeating the mirror render, so a run that just filed 8 issues ends by printing completion over mirrors that do not contain them.
Suggested change: re-run `gen-mirrors.sh .` once at the end of the sweep when at least one candidate was imported, and assert a newly created issue appears in a mirror.

**10. The "nothing to do" line can be false.**
Plan line 1121 increments the counter in `reconcile_config` and the sweep only.
The drift-refresh loop at `setup.sh:75-87` prints a diff and asks per file, and `$TIDY` at `setup.sh:241` prints `byproduct:` and asks per item (confirmed at `scripts/tidy.sh:17-24`).
The brief bought exactly one line here, "finds nothing to do and **says so**" at line 39, so that line is the one that must not be wrong; a run that asked four questions and then claimed nothing to do is worse than the current silence.

## Specifics and rationale

### High severity

**1. `docs/plans/*` unexcluded.**
Covered in full above.
Suggested change: add `docs/plans/*` to the `is_excluded` prefix case in Task 4 step a, rename the test fixture off a plan filename, restate the steady-state count, and record that plan and brief archival stays owned by the Archive-and-graduation rules.

**2. The archive move has no guards.**
Task 4 step a (plan line 1113) specifies only `mkdir -p docs/archive`, then `git mv` when the file is tracked else `mv`.
There is no `-n`, no existence check, and no check that the candidate path is inside the repo.
`skills/loop-setup/setup.sh:33` accepts `--scan <dir>` with no in-tree requirement, and `tests/loop-setup/import.sh:68` already runs `setup.sh --scan "$EXTRA"` where `EXTRA="$(mktemp -d)"`, under `LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1`, with `$EXTRA/extra-plan.md` matching the `plan` keyword.
So the first run of the existing suite after Task 4 lands would `mv` a file out of an unrelated directory into the sandbox repo, and the suite would stay green because it never asserts that `$EXTRA/extra-plan.md` survives.
Separately, two candidates sharing a basename collapse onto one `docs/archive/<name>.md` and the first is destroyed with no message.
Suggested change: skip the move when the destination exists and say so, and skip the archive offer entirely for any candidate whose normalized path is absolute or starts with `../`.

**3. The root `find` pass collides with the empty-`roots` guard.**
`setup.sh:178` is `[ "${#roots[@]}" -gt 0 ] || return 0`, which exists because `find "${roots[@]}"` with an empty array is unsafe.
I confirmed the failure mode by running it: `bash -c 'set -uo pipefail; a=(); find "${a[@]}" -maxdepth 0'` prints `.`, so GNU find silently defaults to the entire tree.
Task 4 step a says only "merged with the existing recursive `find`" and never mentions the guard, so the obvious implementation of a repo with no `docs/` directory is a recursive scan of everything.
Note that `setup.sh:177` already uses the `${SCAN_ROOTS[@]+"${SCAN_ROOTS[@]}"}` idiom for exactly this hazard, which is the in-repo pattern to follow.
Suggested change: run the root pass unconditionally, keep the recursive pass behind the existing guard, and replace the function-level early return with an empty-candidate-list return.

**4. The `LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE` gate is unexpressible as specified.**
Plan lines 1101-1104 say the per-item confirmation "is not satisfied by `LOOP_ASSUME_YES` alone when `MODE` is `github` or `gitlab`" while "local mode and interactive per-item answers are unaffected".
`ask()` at `setup.sh:8-13` returns 0 for `LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1` and for an interactive `y` with no signal distinguishing them.
An implementer with zero context has two readings, and the wrong one (gate on `MODE` being remote) breaks the interactive path the plan promises to leave alone, including Task 7 Steps 2 and 3 in forge.
Task 4's test only exercises the non-interactive path, so the wrong reading passes.
Suggested change: state the condition literally, `[ "${LOOP_ASSUME_YES:-0}" = 1 ] && [ "${LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE:-0}" != 1 ]`.

**5. `--dry-run-remote` stops meaning what it says.**
`setup.sh:224-234` scopes the entire remote finalize on `DRY_REMOTE=1`, and `skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:50` documents the flag as skipping remote calls "instead of calling gh".
The new sweep gate keys on `MODE` and `LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE` with no `DRY_REMOTE` term, so `--dry-run-remote LOOP_ASSUME_YES=1 LOOP_IMPORT_REMOTE=1` files real issues.
Existing dry-run tests do not set `LOOP_ASSUME_YES`, so nothing catches it and the next test author walks into it.
The plan's own review record cut a `DRY_REMOTE` interaction from the migration offer and never applied the same thought to the sweep.
Suggested change: add `[ "$DRY_REMOTE" -eq 0 ]` to the remote-creation condition, print the skip, and correct `SKILL.md:50` in Task 6.

**8. The mode-switch offer has no acknowledgment path.**
Plan line 883 makes a declined switch deliberately non-durable, justified at line 70 by "declines are the rare case once accepts self-archive".
That reasoning is sound for imports and false here: a declined mode switch has no archiving equivalent, so it is the one offer with unbounded repeat and no off switch.
It also reverses a shipped contract: `skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:16` says setup "skips the question entirely (idempotent, never re-asks)" and `:39` says "a declared mode is never re-asked", while `config/repo-state.md:58` actively tells users to choose local deliberately for branched work.
Task 3's own test asserts only the easy half, that an agreeing repo is never nagged (plan line 800).
See the narrowing note below for what I would and would not take here.

**14. The `backlog-group` check cannot fail informatively.**
Plan line 103 declined a reviewer's premise that a top-level group may be unusable on a university-wide instance, and adopted an exit-0 check instead.
The brief records at line 121 that the live group query returns `[]`.
An empty result set makes exit 0 pass identically for a correctly scoped group and for a university-wide one that will later pull other teams' `idea` issues into this repo's declared backlog view.
Plan lines 1592-1593 treat non-zero as the only failure signal, so the wrong-but-working case is unobservable, and the brief itself bins top-level grouping as **Guessed** at lines 143-145.
Suggested change: assert that every returned project path begins with `university-advancement/crm`, and name the fallback derivation as the action on any foreign project.

**15. A declined drift refresh leaves forge lying about its own provenance.**
The drift refresh is per file and declinable at `setup.sh:75-87`, and Task 7 Step 2 presents those refreshes as offers without marking any required.
Task 2's fix lives only in loop-stack's copy of `gen-mirrors.sh`; the vendored copy defaults `SRC_LABEL="GitHub issues"` for every non-local mode at `scripts/gen-mirrors.sh:84-87`.
So accepting the gitlab mode switch while declining the `gen-mirrors.sh` refresh produces mirrors that disclose GitHub as the source of truth on a GitLab repo, in a file whose entire purpose is disclosure, in the exact repo the plan ships to.
Suggested change: have the gitlab finalize fail with a named fix when the target repo's `gen-mirrors.sh` does not contain `GitLab issues`, and mark the `tracker.sh` and `gen-mirrors.sh` refreshes as required for gitlab mode in Task 7 Step 2.
